HomePage.companyBody: Don't wait for applications. Find the right candidates: describe who you're looking for, MIRA shows you who really fits.

faq.q: Why should I use MIRA if I already have LinkedIn?
faq.a: LinkedIn is a social network. You sign up, you're faced with a thousand things, you don't really know what to write or where, you scroll through other people's posts, and in the end your profile just sits there, often filled in badly, because no one guided you. Companies don't know who you really are, or what and when you'd be available for, and being contacted by companies almost never happens. On MIRA it's the opposite: MIRA guides you step by step and in no time your card is ready, capturing who you are, what you've done and in which field, where and when you want to be available.

faq.q: What do associations have to do with it?
faq.a: The associations at your university run their selections on MIRA. Once your MiraCard is complete you can apply directly here: they receive your application together with your profile, they can invite you to an interview and update the status of your application step by step, so you always know where you stand.

Companies registered on MIRA see it anonymously, without anything that identifies you. If one wants to talk to you it sends a contact request: you see who they are, what they're looking for, and you decide. Your identity is revealed only if you accept. Associations see your card only if you apply to them yourself.

faq.q: I'm a first-year with no experience. Does it still make sense?
faq.a: Yes, and probably more than anywhere else. The MiraCard isn't a list of internships: MIRA's questions bring out personal projects, competitions, competitive sport, summer jobs, things you'd never put on a CV that actually say a lot about you.
About five minutes for the essentials. Then you can complete the card at your own pace: the more you share, the more likely a company finds you for the right thing.

faq.q: Do I need a CV ready?
faq.a: No. If you have one you upload it and MIRA starts from there to save you time. If you don't, the card is built by talking.

faq.q: What happens if a company contacts me?
faq.a: You get a request and you see everything: who the company is, what they're looking for and why they chose your profile. You decide whether to accept or decline. If you accept you can chat on the platform, and you choose when to share your contact details. From there the company can invite you to an interview and move the process forward. If you decline, nothing happens: you stay anonymous.
For students yes, and it stays free. We don't sell your data and we don't give it to anyone outside the platform.

HomePage.associationPointApply: Open applications by saying which roles you want and what you want to ask. Applicants arrive with their MiraCard: studies, exams, experience and skills already there, not a CV to decipher.
HomePage.associationPointInterviews: The platform schedules the interviews. You pick the days, everyone on the board marks when they are free, candidates only book where someone actually is. We create the video call link, and confirmations and calendar invites go out on their own.
HomePage.associationPointMembers: Whoever you accept becomes a member of the association: you arrange them into sections by area or role, decide who administers, and the team stays current without spreadsheets.
HomePage.associationPointCompanies: Your members join the pool partner companies search on MIRA. What they build with you stops staying inside the association and starts counting outside.

guide.domande: Last block: do you want to ask candidates specific questions? Their answers arrive together with their MIRA Card. If you don't need any, tick the box and we're done.

AdminUsers.signupLinkIntro: Share this link to have new students register on MIRA (requires an institutional university email).

AdminUsers.reminderMessageDefault:
Hi {name},

OnboardingFlow.linkedinSteps:
The LinkedIn PDF is the fastest route: it already contains experiences, education and skills.
1. Open LinkedIn in a browser (it cannot be done from the app) and go to your profile
2. Click the three dots under your name
3. Choose "Save to PDF"
4. Upload the file here
OnboardingFlow.cvReadError: I couldn't fully read your CV: check the experiences below and fix them by hand.
OnboardingFlow.hintBocconi: You can download it from you@b: in the certificates/self-certifications section you'll find the self-certification with your exam list.
OnboardingFlow.hintGeneric: You can usually find it on your university's website or student portal, under documents and certificates.
OnboardingFlow.guideHeader: Last step to unlock applications: your degree details. I already took university and level from your sign-up, check they are right and add course and years, then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideEsperienze: Now your experiences. Three quick ways to add them: upload your CV, download your LinkedIn profile as a PDF (I will show you how), or add them by hand below. Remember that personal projects, sport, volunteering and student associations all count: anything that says something about you.
OnboardingFlow.guideEsperienzeManual: Fine, let's build them by hand: add your experiences below. Personal projects, sport, volunteering and student associations all count. Write the descriptions however they come out, ✦ Improve with MIRA rewrites them in English, CV style. Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideEsperienzeAfterCV: I found {count, plural, =0 {your experiences} one {1 experience} other {# experiences}} in your CV and prepared them below in English. Review them, fix them or add more, including the ones you'd never put on a CV (projects, sports, volunteering, association activities). Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideDisponibilitaIntro:
Hi {name}! I am MIRA: let's build your MIRA Card together. You need it to apply to associations, and it is the profile companies will use to find and contact you (it will be in English, I take care of the translation).

Let's start from what you are looking for: use the toggle to tell me whether you are searching or open to opportunities, and fill in the fields (type of experience, field, dates and place). Below, tell me your career plan: what your next steps in study or training are, which role you would like to step into right after, and where you aim to get in the long run. If you are still exploring, that is perfectly fine. Write the way you speak!

✦ Improve with MIRA turns it into English. Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideLingue: Which languages do you know? Add them below with level and any certification (e.g. English, C1, IELTS 7.5). Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideLingueWithCV: I've already added the languages found in your CV below: check levels and certifications, add any missing ones, then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.guideProfilo:
Now the part that's usually missing from CVs: how you present yourself beyond exams and experiences. No hobby lists, no interview-style lines, tell me something authentic:
• What do you follow on your own, outside your course syllabi?
• Outside your studies, what do you do consistently?
• How would people who know you well describe you?
• What can't you stand at work or in your studies, or what would you never give up?
• What's the most "you" thing you've done in the last year?
Write the way you speak, Italian is fine too: ✦ Improve with MIRA turns it into a first-person text in English. Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.gateBody: Your card is at {pct}%: you can already apply to associations on MIRA. Or we can complete the last sections in a few minutes.
OnboardingFlow.gateWarning: NOTE: The more complete your profile, the more you attract companies' attention!
OnboardingFlow.finalBody: You will find it in the Profile section and you can edit it whenever you want.
OnboardingFlow.guideCompetenze: In this section add your hard skills: software and tools (Excel, Python, SQL, Bloomberg, Figma), methods you have actually applied (company valuation, financial statement analysis), techniques picked up on the job. For each one give your level and where you learned it. Then press Confirm.
OnboardingFlow.finalNext1: You can apply to associations at your university: instead of a CV, they read your MIRA Card.
OnboardingFlow.finalNext2: Companies search on MIRA by describing the profile they want. If your card matches they find you, but they see an anonymous profile: your name and contacts are yours to share, only if you accept the request.
OnboardingFlow.finalNext3: The more complete your card, the more searches find you. Update it when you pass an exam or start something new.
OnboardingFlow.guideEsamiTriennale:
Want to show what you studied? Upload your transcript (the record listing your exams and grades): it is the concrete proof of the subjects you covered and the theoretical grounding you have. The system works out your GPA automatically.

With the toggles below, you decide whether to show or hide both your GPA and the individual exam grades.
OnboardingFlow.guideEsamiMagistrale:
Want to show what you studied? Your transcript (the record listing your exams and grades) shows companies the subjects you covered hands-on and your theoretical grounding. The system works out your GPA automatically.

If you have them at hand, you can upload two documents: your current transcript, for the exams you are taking now in your Master's, and your Bachelor's one, to show your previous path too.

With the toggles below, you decide whether to show or hide both your GPA and the individual exam grades.
OnboardingFlow.skipEsamiNote: You can upload it whenever you want from your Profile, the card updates on its own.

Footer.tagline: The profile your campus associations and companies use to find you.

Interviews.subhead: One round for each stage of your selection. Pick the days and hours when the association runs interviews, then everyone on the board marks when they are available, and invited candidates book a time where somebody is there.
Interviews.noCycles: You need an application cycle first: interviews belong to a cycle.
Interviews.noSessions: No interview sessions yet. Create one to start.
Interviews.descriptionPlaceholder: What to expect: how long, how to prepare, who will be there.
Interviews.linkModePerInterview: A different link for each interview
Interviews.linkModePerInterviewHint: You create it and paste it after the candidate books. You will find it in the booked interviews list.
Interviews.linkModeSharedHint: One room, reused for every interview. Fine if you run one at a time.
Interviews.requiredInterviewersLabel: How many from the board must attend
Interviews.availabilityIntro: Mark the times you can run interviews: click a slot, or use "Whole day". The rest of the board shows next to it, each in their own colour. Candidates can only book where somebody is there.
Interviews.stepNoAvailability: Nobody from the board has given their availability yet.
Interviews.bookedEmpty: Nobody has booked a time yet.
Interviews.howItWorks: How it works: here you set the days and hours of the round. Once created, you and the rest of the board mark when you are available. A time only becomes bookable when somebody is there, and the candidates you invite pick from those.
Interviews.requiredInterviewersHint: Usually one. Set two and a time opens to candidates only when at least two people are available.
Interviews.placeModeSharedHint: One room for every interview in the round.
Interviews.placeModePerInterview: A different place for each interview
Interviews.placeModePerInterviewHint: You set it after the candidate books, from the booked interviews list.
Interviews.noRoundsForCurrent: No interview rounds for {cycle} yet. Create one to start inviting candidates.
Interviews.noOpenSelection: No selection is open. Open one from the Cycles tab to create rounds.
Interviews.stepInviteCandidates: Ready: invite candidates and they will pick a time.
Interviews.archivedRound: This round belongs to a closed selection: it stays here as history and cannot be changed.
Interviews.placeBeforeInviteHint: Set it now and the candidate gets one single email with time and place. Otherwise you will have to send it later, one interview at a time.
Interviews.linkModeAutoHint: When a candidate books, MIRA creates a video call link just for that interview and sends it right away to them and to whoever runs it, inside the same email as the time. You do not have to create or paste anything. We use Jitsi Meet, a free video call service that opens in the browser, on phones too, with nothing to install and no account: you click the link and you are in. The room has a long random address, so only whoever got the email can reach it.
Interviews.daysExplainer: Pick the days the association runs interviews. No need to be precise: afterwards everyone on the board marks the hours they are actually there, and times with nobody available never show up to candidates.
Interviews.hoursLabel: Time range, the same for every day
Interviews.hoursHint: This is not the window you all have to be there: it is the span interviews can fall into. The real hours are what each person marks on their own availability.
Interviews.previewTimeNote: The candidate picks the time among those the board covers.
Interviews.previewPlaceAuto: video call link generated when they book
Interviews.previewPlaceLater: you tell them the place after they book
Interviews.stepUpcoming: {upcoming, plural, one {1 interview to run} other {# interviews to run}}
Interviews.stepUpcomingAndDone: {upcoming, plural, one {1 interview to run} other {# interviews to run}}, {done, plural, one {1 already done} other {# already done}}
Interviews.stepAllDone: {done, plural, one {1 interview done, none scheduled} other {# interviews done, none scheduled}}

StudentInterviews.pageSubtitle: This is where interviews from the associations you applied to show up. When one invites you, you pick the time among the free ones: as soon as you book we send the confirmation with the place or the link, and the calendar invite.
StudentInterviews.pickPrompt: Pick the time that works best for you.
StudentInterviews.canReschedule: You can still change time by picking another one below.
StudentInterviews.linkComingLater: The association will send you the link before the interview.
StudentInterviews.noSlotsLeft: No times available right now. The association will get in touch.
StudentInterviews.bookingsClosed: Bookings for this round are closed.
StudentInterviews.confirmBook: Confirm your interview on {date}? We send you the confirmation by email.

CandidateNotes.heading: Board notes
CandidateNotes.explainer: Internal notes on this candidate: impressions from the interview, doubts, things to check. The candidate never sees them. Grouped by who wrote them.

Profile.intro: Your account: how other people see you and what you choose to show. What you tell about yourself lives in your MiraCard instead.
Profile.photoIntro: A photo turns your application into a person rather than a name. It is not required and you can remove it whenever you want.
Profile.photoFormats: JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 4 MB

photoSeenAssociations.what: They see it on your MiraCard when you apply, next to your name.

photoSeenCompanies.what: They do not. To them you are a profile without a name until you share your contact details.

photoSeenPublic.what: Nobody: your MiraCard is not a public page and never reaches search engines.

Profile.accountHint: To change your name, email or university write to privacy@mirajob.cloud: these are how associations recognise you, so they are not editable on your own.
Profile.gradesIntro: Your weighted average and individual grades are hidden by default. The exams you have taken are visible either way: what you decide here is whether the grades show too.
Profile.gradesAssociationsHint: Average and grades visible to the associations you apply to
Profile.gradesCompaniesHint: Average and grades visible to companies

dataWho.a: MIRA, on Supabase servers in Europe. We do not sell it and we do not pass it to anyone you have not chosen.

dataAssociations.a: Only if you apply to them: your MiraCard with name, photo, studies, experience and skills. Associations you do not apply to cannot see you.

dataCompanies.a: A profile with no name, photo or contact details. They get your name and contacts only when you say yes.

dataRights.a: A copy of everything we hold about you, a correction of anything wrong, or the deletion of your account. Write to us and we answer within thirty days.

Profile.phoneHint: Optional. It only matters if you choose to show it, below.
Profile.emailLocked: Your email is your login: to change it write to privacy@mirajob.cloud, so we can verify the new address before switching.
Profile.passwordIntro: Change it whenever you want. We ask for the current one first.
Profile.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
Profile.contactIntro: Email and phone are hidden by default. Here you choose who sees them.
Profile.phoneAssociationsHint: Visible to the associations you apply to
Profile.phoneCompaniesHint: There is no switch here: companies get your contact details only if you accept one of their requests, and you choose what to share right then.
